parole.testo: From Proto-Iranian *āmaH-, from Proto-Iranian *ā- + *maH- (“to measure”), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *maH-, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂éd (“at”) + *meh₁- (“to measure”). Compare آماده (âmâde, “ready”), Avestan 𐬁𐬨𐬁𐬙𐬀- (āmāta-), Sanskrit माति (māti, “measure, knowledge”), Ancient Greek μῆτῐς (mêtĭs, “sk
From Proto-Iranian *Hárǰati, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *Hárǰʰati, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂elgʷʰ-.
From Proto-Iranian [Term?], from Proto-Indo-Iranian [Term?]. Cognate with Sanskrit अणक (aṇaka, “contemptible, insignificant”).
From Proto-Iranian *Hángištah, from Proto-Iranian *Hángārah, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *Hángāras, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁óngʷl̥ (“charcoal”).

Ultimately from Proto-Iranian *varn-aka-, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *wr̥Hánas, from Proto-Indo-European *urh₁en- (“ram”). See also Mazanderani وره (vare), Sanskrit उरण (úraṇa), Central Kurdish بەرخ (berx), Northern Kurdish berx, Zazaki verek, Baluchi گْوّرگ (gwarag), Ancient Greek ἀρήν (arḗn), Old Arm
From Proto-Iranian *band-, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *bʰandʰ-, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *bʰendʰ- (“to bind”); cognate to English bend, bind.

parole.significato: band, tie, fastening, ligature, bandage, chain, shackle, fetter
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Persian *bandah, from Proto-Iranian *bandáh, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *bʰandʰás, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *bʰendʰ- (“to bind”). Compare Old Armenian բանտ (bant, “prison”), an Iranian borrowing. More at band, bind. Doublet of باند (bând).

From Middle Persian [Term?] ŠPYL / wyh (weh, “better, good”), from Old Persian *vahuš (“good”), from Proto-Iranian *Hwáhuš, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *Hwásuš, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₁wésus (“good”). Northern Luri بێ (bı). Related to Old Armenian վեհ (veh, “sublime”), an Iranian borrowin
Inherited from Middle Persian [script needed] (wck' /⁠waččag⁠/, “child, baby, cub”), from Proto-Iranian *wacáh (“calf”).
Inherited from Proto-Iranian *tāp-, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *tāpás, from Proto-Indo-European *tep-.

From Proto-Iranian, from Proto-Indo-Iranian, from Proto-Indo-European *(s)ptyēw- (“to spit, vomit”). Akin to Ossetian ту (tu, “spittle”), Sanskrit ष्ठीवति (ṣṭhīvati, “to spit”), Armenian թուք (tʻukʻ, “spit, spittle”), Serbo-Croatian pljuvati (“to spit”), Ancient Greek πτύω (ptúō, “to spit out”), Lat
From Proto-Iranian *tafšcáti, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *tapsćáti, from Proto-Indo-European *tep- (“to be warm, tepid”).

From Proto-Iranian *tánHtā, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *tánHtar-, from Proto-Indo-European *ténh₂-tōr or *tónh₂-tōr, whence Latin tonitrus may also be derived; ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *(s)tenh₂- (“to thunder, resound”). Compare similarly *tónh₂-r̥, whence Germanic and Celtic cognates. Cogna

From Proto-Iranian *taw(H)táH, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *taw(H)táH (“people, folk, crowd”), from Proto-Indo-European *tew(H)téh₂ (“people, tribe, men-at-arms”). Cognate with Northern Kurdish tûde, Sogdian 𐫤𐫇𐫔𐫏𐫍 (twδyh /⁠tūδē⁠/). More distantly related to Latin tōtus, Latvian tàuta, Lithuanian tautà,

parole.significato: to search; to seek; to look for
parole.testo: From Proto-Iranian *Hyawd- (“to fight, struggle (for something), strive, seek”), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *Hyawdʰ- (“to fight, struggle”).
Inherited from Proto-Iranian *Hhučiθráh (composed of *Hhu- (“good”) and *čiθráh (“appearance, likeness; face”)), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *Hsučitrás.
Inherited from Proto-Iranian *Hhúškah, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *Hsúškas, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂sews- + *-kos. Cognate with Sanskrit शुष्क (śuṣka).

Inherited from Proto-Iranian *hwanH- (“to call”), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *swanH-, from Proto-Indo-European *swenh₂- (“to sound”). Compare Northern Kurdish xwendin, Northern Luri هںنێ (hənı), Latin sonō, Sanskrit स्वनति (svanati).

From Middle Persian 𐭧𐭥𐭡 (xūb), from Old Persian *huvāpah, from Proto-Iranian *HhuHā́pah, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *HsuHápas, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁su- (“good”) + *h₃épos (“work”). Compare Sogdian [script needed] (xwp).
Inherited from Proto-Iranian *húHar, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *súHar, from Proto-Indo-European *sóh₂wl̥.
Inherited from Proto-Iranian *dā́ru, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *dā́ru, from Proto-Indo-European *dóru. Also see دار (dār /dâr), درخت (daraxt). Aghwan 𐔳𐕒𐕡𐕙𐕒𐕡𐔳 (durud) is an Iranian borrowing.

From Middle Persian [script needed] (dwšmn'), [script needed] (dwšmyn'), 𐫅𐫇𐫢𐫖𐫏𐫗 (dwšmyn /⁠dušmēn⁠/, “enemy”), from Proto-Iranian *dušmánāh. Compare Ancient Greek δῠσμενής (dŭsmenḗs), Sanskrit दुर्मनस् (durmanas).

From Middle Persian 𐭣𐭩𐭫 (dyl /⁠dil⁠/), from Proto-Iranian *jā́rd, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *ȷ́ʰā́rd, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *ḱḗr; with a regular phonetic shift *ȷ́ŕ̥d- > *dŕ̥d > *dŕ̥l > dil. For the phonetic change, compare گل (gol) and سالار (sâlâr). Cognates with Parthian 𐫉𐫏𐫡𐫅 (zyrd /⁠
From Proto-Iranian *danHáyati, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *dʰanHáyati, from Proto-Indo-European *dʰenh₂-. Cognate with Sanskrit धन् (dhan, “to cause to move”).
From Proto-Iranian *duHmáh, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *dʰuHmás, from Proto-Indo-European *dʰuh₂mós. Compare Northern Kurdish dû and Lurish دی (di, “smoke”).

Inherited from Proto-Iranian *duHráh (“far”), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *duHrás (“far”), from Proto-Indo-European *dweh₂rós, from *dweh₂- + *-rós. Cognate with Central Kurdish دوور (dûr, “far, distant”), Northern Luri دیر (dir), Pashto لرې (lëre, “distant”), Sanskrit दूर (dūra, “distant, remote”), Ave

parole.significato: coloured red and white; spotted red or white.
parole.testo: Ultimately from Proto-Iranian *ra(n)ǰ- (“to colour, dye”) (compare Sogdian [script needed] (rɣš- /⁠raxš⁠/, “Rakhsh”), Khwarezmian رختک (rxtk /⁠raxtak⁠/, “red”), Mazanderani رش (raš, “reddish-brown”), Northern Kurdish reş (“black”), Talysh رش (rəş, “light brown”)), from Proto-Indo-Iranian (compare Sa

From Proto-Iranian *raz- (“to leave, escape (one's notice)”), related to Proto-Indo-Iranian *raȷ́ʰ- (“to abandon”). Cognate with Sanskrit रहति (rahati, “to abandon”) and रहस्य (rahasya, “mystery”); see the latter for more.
From Proto-Iranian *Hráwdah, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *Hráwdʰas, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁lewdʰ- (“to grow”). Indo-Iranian cognates include Baluchi ردگ (ruddag) and Sanskrit रोधति (rodhati).

From Proto-Iranian *wrais- (“to turn, to spin”), from Proto-Indo-Iranian, from Proto-Indo-European *wriḱ-yé-ti (“to twist, to bend”), whence also Avestan 𐬎𐬭𐬎𐬎𐬌𐬯𐬌𐬀 (uruuisia, “to turn”), German reihen (“to sew loosely”), English wry, Latin rīca (“veil”). Doublet of رشته (rešte, “thread, string”).

From Proto-Iranian *ra(n)ǰ- (“to colour, dye”), from Proto-Indo-Iranian [Term?]. Cognate with Sanskrit रञ्ज् (rañj, “to be dyed or coloured, to redden, grow red, glow”). Related to رنگ (rang, “color”).
From Proto-Iranian *Hrawtáh, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *Hrawtás.
From Proto-Iranian *jyáh, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *ȷ́ʰyás.

From Proto-Iranian *jā́nu, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *ȷ́ā́nu, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵónu. Cognate with Mazanderani زندی (zendi), Ancient Greek γόνυ (gónu), Latin genū, English knee. Doublet of گونیا.
From Proto-Iranian [Term?], from Proto-Indo-Iranian [Term?], from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰer-, *gʰer- (“to encircle; to spin around”).
From Proto-Iranian [Term?], from Proto-Indo-Iranian [Term?], from Proto-Indo-European *ǵerh₂- (“to grow old, to mature”).
From Proto-Iranian *jaluš, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *ȷ́aluš, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵelu-. Akin to Old Armenian տզրուկ (tzruk), an Iranian borrowing.
Ultimately from Proto-Iranian *jar-, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *ȷ́ar-, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵwelH- (“to burn, shine”). Compare Proto-Germanic *kulą (“coal”), Irish gual (“coal”).

From Proto-Iranian *ǰáyHati, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *ǰáyHati, from Proto-Indo-European *gʷéyh₃eti (“to live”), from the root *gʷeyh₃-. Cognate with Avestan 𐬘𐬎𐬎𐬀𐬌𐬙𐬌 (juuaⁱti), Northern Kurdish jîyan, Pashto ژوند کول (žwënd kawël), Sanskrit जीवति (jīvati). More distantly related to Ancient Greek βείο

From Proto-Iranian *snušáH, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *snušáH, from Proto-Indo-European *snusós (“daughter-in-law”). Cognate with Sanskrit स्नुषा (snuṣā́, “daughter-in-law”), Latin nurus, Ancient Greek νυός (nuós), Old English snoru.
Ultimately derived from Proto-Iranian *cráwniš, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *ćráwniš, from Proto-Indo-European *ḱlównis.

Inherited from Proto-Iranian *gžárati, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *gžʰárati, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *dʰgʷʰéreti (“to flow, to melt”). Cognate with Avestan 𐬖𐬲𐬀𐬭𐬀𐬌𐬙𐬌 (γžaraⁱti), Ancient Greek φθείρω (phtheírō) and Sanskrit क्षरति (kṣarati, “to flow, stream, trickle”).

From Proto-Iranian *hmarati- (“to remember, recall, count”) (possibly with a prefix of unknown origin), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *smárati (“to remember, recollect”). Indo-Iranian cognates include Central Kurdish ژماردن (jmardin, “to count”), Pashto شمېرل (śmerël, “to count”), and Sanskrit स्मरति (smá
From Proto-Iranian *-mánts (possessive suffix), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *-mánts, from Proto-Indo-European *-ménts. Cognate with Avestan -𐬨𐬀𐬥𐬝 (-mant̰) and Sanskrit -मत् (-mat).

parole.significato: a suffix used to form adjectives and nouns with the meaning of "pertaining to" or "depending on"
parole.testo: From Proto-Iranian *-wánts, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *-wánts, from Proto-Indo-European *-wénts. Cognate with Sanskrit -वत् (-vat).
From Proto-Iranian *lagžnáh, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *slagžʰnás.

From Proto-Iranian *langa-, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *langa- (“lame”); according to Pokorny, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *(s)leh₁g- (“feeble, weak”). Cognate with Central Kurdish لەنگ (leng), Pashto [script needed] (lang), Sanskrit लङ्ग (laṅga, “lame”).

Inherited from Proto-Iranian *luxšáh, Proto-Indo-Iranian *lukšás, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *lówksneh₂ (“moon”), derived from the root *lewk- (“bright, to shine, to see”). Cognates include Old Armenian լուսին (lusin, “moon”), Proto-Slavic *luna and Old Latin losna.

From Middle Persian [Book Pahlavi needed] (mzg /⁠mazg⁠/, “brain, marrow”), from Proto-Iranian *mazgáh, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *mazgʰás, from Proto-Indo-European *mosgʰos. Cognate of Russian мозг (mozg), Serbo-Croatian мозак (mozak) and English marrow.

Inherited from Proto-Iranian *HmíčaH, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *Hmíkš, from Proto-Indo-European *h₃meygʰ-. Cognates with English mist, Vedic Sanskrit मिह् (mih, “fog, mist”), Ancient Greek ὀμίχλη (omíkhlē, “fog, mist”), Polish mgła (“fog, mist, haze”), and Lithuanian miglà (“mist, haze”). Related to

parole.significato: joint (Any part of the body where two bones join)
parole.testo: From a derivative of Proto-Iranian *muštiš (“fist”) (with sound change št > č), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *muštíš (“fist”).

PIE word  *h₃nṓgʰs Inherited from Proto-Iranian *Hnāxunah, a derivative of *Hnā́xš, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *Hnā́kš, from Proto-Indo-European *h₃nṓgʰs. Compare Indo-Iranian cognates Central Kurdish نینۆک (nînok), Northern Kurdish neynok, Baluchi ناہن (náhun) / ناکن (nákun), Sanskrit न॒ख (nakhá).
Ultimately from Proto-Iranian *namráh, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *namrás (“submissive, humble”).

From Proto-Iranian *ni- + *wač- (“to say, speak”). The prefix is from Proto-Iranian *ní (“down”), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *ní (“down, into”), while the second component is from Proto-Indo-European *wekʷ- (“to speak, sound out”).
Inherited from Proto-Iranian *Hnawatí, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *Hnawatí, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁newn̥tí, from *h₁néwn̥ + *tí.

PIE word  *wáy From Proto-Iranian *wáy, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *wáy, eventually from Proto-Indo-European *wáy. Cognate with Latin vae, English woe. Similar words also exist in Semitic, compare Aramaic וָי (wāy), Arabic وَيْلٌ (waylun).

From Proto-Iranian *pačati, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *páčati, from Proto-Indo-European *pekʷ- (“to cook, become ripe”). Cognates with Mazanderani بپتن (bapeten), Baluchi پچگ (pačag, “to fry, bake”), Northern Kurdish pêtin, Yaghnobi пухсак (puxsak).

From Middle Persian [Term?] (/⁠purr⁠/), from Proto-Iranian *pr̥Hnáh (compare Northern Kurdish pirr (“much, very, many”), Central Kurdish پڕ (pirr, “full”)), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *pr̥Hnás (compare Old Avestan 𐬞𐬆𐬭𐬆𐬥𐬀 (pər^əna), from Proto-Indo-European *pl̥h₁nós (compare Russian по́лный (pólnyj), L

From Proto-Iranian [Term?], from Proto-Indo-Iranian *parnám, from Proto-Indo-European *pornóm (“feather, wing”), from *perH- (“to fly”). Cognate with Avestan 𐬞𐬀𐬭𐬆𐬥𐬀 (par^əna, “feather”), Sanskrit पर्ण (parṇá, “feather”), Lithuanian spar̃nas (“wing”), Old Church Slavonic перо (pero, “wing, feather”),

From Proto-Iranian, from Proto-Indo-Iranian. Cognate with Sogdian [script needed] (prγrs’y /⁠parγarsē⁠/, “round, oval”), Northern Kurdish pergal (“mode, system, order”), Sanskrit प्रकार (prakāra, “sort, kind, form, nature, way, mode, manner”). The first element is from Proto-Iranian *pari- (“around”

From Proto-Iranian *pášma, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *páćšma (“hair, bristles”), from Proto-Indo-European *poḱ-s-mn̥ (“hair, whiskers”), from *peḱ- (“to shear, pluck”). Cognate with Avestan 𐬞𐬀𐬱𐬨𐬀𐬥 (pašman), Sanskrit पक्ष्मन् (pakṣman).

Inherited from Middle Persian [script needed] (pnc /⁠panǰ⁠/), from Proto-Iranian *pánča, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *pánča, from Proto-Indo-European *pénkʷe. Compare Northern Kurdish pênc, Ossetian фондз (fonʒ), Pashto پنځه (pindzə), Avestan 𐬞𐬀𐬧𐬗𐬀 (paṇca), Sanskrit पञ्च (páñca), Sarikoli pundz.

From Proto-Iranian *puH- (“to rot”), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *puH-, from Proto-Indo-European *puH- (“rotten, foul”). Compare Sanskrit पूयति (pūyati, “to stink, to become putrid”), Latin pūs (“pus, foul matter”), Ancient Greek πῡ́θω (pū́thō, “to rot, to decay”).

Inherited from Proto-Iranian *pari-yāhana-, from Proto-Iranian *pari- (“around, peri-”) + *yaHs- (“to girdle, gird”). Northern Luri پیرںن (pirən). From Proto-Iranian *jánukah, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *ȷ́ʰánuš, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵénus (“chin, jaw, cheek”). Cognates include Avestan 𐬰𐬁𐬥𐬎 (zānu), Sanskrit हनु (hánu), Armenian ծնոտ (cnot), Latin gena, Tocharian A śanweṃ, Welsh gen, Dutch kin, English chin, German Kinn.
From Proto-Iranian *čaxrákah (“spinning wheel”), derived from *čaxrám (“wheel”), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *čakrám (“wheel”). Compare Old Armenian ճախարակ (čaxarak).
From Proto-Iranian *čaxrám (“wheel”), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *čakrám (“wheel”).

From Proto-Iranian *čárHati, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *čárHati, from Proto-Indo-European *kʷel- (“to move; to turn (around)”). Indo-Iranian cognates include Ossetian цӕрын (cæryn, “to live”), Pashto څرېدل (śaredal, “to pasture, graze”), Avestan 𐬗𐬀𐬭𐬁𐬥𐬍 (carānī, “I move, approach”), and Sanskrit चरति (

From Proto-Iranian *custáh, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *čutˢtás, from Proto-Indo-European *(s)kud-tó-s (“propelled”), from *(s)kewd- (“to shoot, throw”). Cognate with Sanskrit चोदति (códati, “to impel”).

From Proto-Iranian *čam- (“to walk”), perhaps a blend of Proto-Iranian *čarH- (“to come and go, wander”) and *gam- (“to come”), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *čálH- (“to move, wander”) + Proto-Indo-European *gʷem- (“to step, come”) respectively. Compare Baluchi چمگ (čamag, “to shake, dance”), Parthian [sc

From Proto-Iranian *čiš-čid / *čiš-čit, from Proto-Iranian *čiš + a suffix *čit of unknown, possibly reduplicative, origin. The former component is from Proto-Indo-Iranian *kíš, from Proto-Indo-European *kʷís, *kʷos (“who, which, what”).

PIE word  *kwŕ̥mis From Proto-Iranian *kŕ̥miš, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *kŕ̥miš, from Proto-Indo-European *kʷŕ̥mis (“worm”). Cognate with Sanskrit कृमि (kṛ́mi, “worm”), Proto-Slavic *čьrvь (“worm”), Lithuanian kirmi̇̀s (“worm”).
From Middle Persian [Book Pahlavi needed] (kšwk' /⁠kašawag⁠/, “tortoise”), from Proto-Iranian *kacyápah. Cognate with Sanskrit कच्छप (kacchapa).

parole.significato: to pull, to drag, to haul
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Iranian *káršati (“to draw, plough”), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *káršati, from Proto-Indo-European *kʷéls-ti, from *kʷels- (“to pull, drag”). Cognate with Avestan 𐬐𐬀𐬭𐬱𐬀𐬌𐬙𐬌 (karšaⁱti) and Sanskrit कर्षति (karṣati). Also compare Old Armenian քարշ (kʻarš), an Iranian borrowing. Relat

Inherited from Proto-Iranian *gáHma, from Proto-Indo-Iranian *gáHma, from Proto-Indo-European *gʷéh₂-mn̥ ~ *gʷh₂-mén-s, from *gʷeh₂- (“to step”). Cognate with Baluchi گام, Avestan 𐬔𐬁𐬨𐬀𐬥 (gāman), Northern Kurdish gav, Ancient Greek βῆμα (bêma), Sanskrit प्रगामन् (pragāman).

From Proto-Iranian *graθH- (“to tie (a knot)”), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *grantH- (“to tie (a knot)”), and cognate with Sanskrit ग्रन्थ् (granth, “to tie (a knot)”) and with Northern Kurdish girê (“knot”) with further origin uncertain. The traditional derivation from Proto-Indo-European *gre(n)tH- (“

Inherited from Proto-Iranian, from Proto-Indo-Iranian, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *glew-. Cognate with Northern Kurdish girover, gilover (“round”), Northern Luri گوڶٮه (gollə, “bullet”), Sanskrit ग्लौ (glau, “lump”).

Probably from Proto-Iranian *wi- (“apart”) + *maiH- (“to harm, damage, fade, decrease”). The prefix is from Proto-Indo-Iranian *wí, from Proto-Indo-European *wí (“apart, away”), and the latter component is from Proto-Indo-European *meyH- (“to lessen, diminish”), from *mey- (“small, little”).
